title: Word: Copilot Chat edit mode creates and edits documents for users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
summary: Pass: the roadmap facts, default-on state and Integrated Apps path are supported, and the briefing distinguishes broad Chat controls from an Edit-mode-specific switch. The licensing notes should name Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic), the in-app experience, rather than rely on the inclusion of standalone Copilot Chat (Basic).

claims.fix: Keep model included. Replace the Copilot Chat (Basic) sentence in licensing.notes with: "Learn describes Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) as the in-app experience for users without the Copilot add-on, including drafting and rewriting in Word; some features have fair use limits." In rationale: cost, replace the standalone Basic clause with "Learn places in-app Word capabilities under Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) for users without the Copilot add-on". The body already makes this distinction, supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-overview.
